data.description:
## Context / Problem
The review gates currently read effective criteria and routing through multiple seams. Code review then consults packaged-only overlay and detector registries, so a project disable or retune can be ignored and an activated project DET criterion can disappear. Separate reads can also describe different repository policy states. RP-06 requires one immutable authority before any selection or model call.

## Approach
Create a repository-bound `CriteriaSnapshot` in `rebar.llm.criteria`. It compiles effective built-ins, project LLM criteria, project DET criteria, prompt/routing/posture/applicability metadata, source locations, and one deterministic digest from the provided repository root and already-resolved operation inputs. Consumers receive the snapshot; they do not reread ambient policy.

Keep applicability vocabularies gate-specific. For project code-review LLM criteria, validate `applies_to` as a non-empty list of non-empty repository-relative globs and define `["**"]` as repository-wide. No changed path match produces a typed non-applicable selection reason. Built-in secondary triggers remain unchanged, project DET selection remains detector-owned, and plan review retains `applies_at` and `trigger`. Migrate `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` entry `project.review-phase-boundaries` from `[]` to `["**"]` so its current all-review behavior is explicit.

Record an ADR describing snapshot ownership, gate-specific applicability, the explicit global-glob spelling, and why a single effective authority is preferable to gate-specific registry reads. The snapshot is data and policy only; it does not interpret YAML/BPMN topology, execute criteria, or decide verdicts.

## Migration and Rollback
Add the snapshot alongside existing registry readers. Golden contract tests compare the snapshot-derived selection inputs with current behavior when no project overlay is present and allow only the approved corrections for effective disables/retunes, project DET inclusion, and project LLM applicability. Existing registry APIs remain as compatibility adapters until the dependent cutover stories land; rollback is a code revert, not a new configuration flag.

## Testing
Use in-process unit and real producer-to-consumer contract tests. One tier lower is insufficient because the known defects occur between the overlay producer and packaged-routing consumers. Tests feed real project routing files through the loader and snapshot compiler, then assert exact selected policy, source provenance, and digest behavior. Negative controls cover built-in empty secondary triggers and plan-review routing, which must not adopt the new project-LLM glob rule.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A real project overlay compiled through `CriteriaSnapshot` yields one immutable digest-bound view containing effective built-in, project LLM, and project DET policy with source provenance.
- [ ] A project code-review LLM criterion with an empty, missing, non-list, or blank `applies_to` fails before any model call with its criterion id, configuration location, and the remedy `use ["**"] for repository-wide`.
- [ ] Given root, nested, and dot paths, `applies_to: ["**"]` selects the criterion exactly once; a nonmatching scoped glob records non-applicable selection without executing it.
- [ ] `.rebar/criteria_routing.json` declares `project.review-phase-boundaries.applies_to` as `["**"]`, and a contract test proves its review membership is unchanged by the migration.
- [ ] Contract tests prove effective built-in disables/retunes and activated project DET entries are present in the snapshot while built-in secondary-trigger and plan-review routing semantics remain unchanged.
- [ ] An ADR documents snapshot ownership, digest inputs, gate-specific applicability, compatibility adapters, and the revert-based rollback.
data.title: RP-06 S1 — Compile immutable effective review-policy snapshots
